body:
So about the last sentence. Let's take https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/95847 as example. If not set, the id of item is dynamically chosen based on it's index. So the id of an item can be 0 if it's index is 0. However since the initialization is dynamic the default value used for serialization purposes is the default (implicit) integer value `0` (it's horrible UX to use dynamic init for something in the inspector like this, but that's not the point.) The implicit default and the dynamic initialization can be identical.

So let's take the following chain of actions:
- add item A: -> index = 0 -> id = 0
- add item B: -> index = 1 -> id = 1
- move item A after item B -> index = 1, id stays 0
- save the scene -> id of A does not get saved since it overlaps with the implicit default, even though the dynamic initialization would initialize to a different value
- load the scene -> the id of A has changed to 1, since after rerunning the dynamic init in the new context it resulted in a different value.

So in this case we set the flag to always serialize the property value. Regardless of the implicit integer default.

If you can pack that in a good sentence that's understandable feel free to do so! I did the best I could :sweat_smile:
